recipes.name: Citrus Shortbread Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon grated orange zest, or more to taste

steps.text: Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl; set aside.
Beat the butter and confectioners' sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Stir in the vanilla and almond extracts and orange zest.
Mix in the flour mixture until just incorporated. Fold in the cranberries; mixing just enough to evenly combine.
Divide the dough into 2 equal portions, then roll into logs about 7 inches long. Wrap each log in wax paper or plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Remove wax paper, and cut the cookie dough into 1/2-inch slices.
Arrange the slices on a baking sheet about 1 inch apart.
Bake in the preheated oven until firm but not browned, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Citrus Shortbread Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Orange zest and dried cranberries give these classic shortbread cookies an extra zing.

video.description: A splendid, soft treat that is as delectable as is gorgeous with the dried cranberries mixed with white shortbread.

review.reviewBody: These are wonderful! They were zesty, fuity with a wonderful texture. I only made two small changes: As another reviewer, I only used 1 cup of chopped cranberries which we found to be plenty! Also, I never had any almond extract so I decided to add 1/4 cup of toasted crushed almond slices. I am not a hugh fan of almond extact but using the real toasted almonds was amazing and really made a difference. Since it said to divide the dough into two logs I decided to add the almonds (1/8 cup for half the recipe) to one log and omit them in the other to test the difference. The cookies without the almonds tasted more fruity...you could really taste the orange and cranberry. The almonds added a more comlex and interesting flavor where all the flavors came through and none were overpowering. We liked both but the cookies with the almonds were our favorite! To toast the almonds: spread sliced almonds on a baking sheet and bake in a 375 deg oven for 3-5min until they look lightly browned. Let cool and crush.

I have made this recipe twice this week. Here is my possible explanation for why some feel the cookies are too dry or crumbly. I used the hint a reviewer suggested & stirred 3 T. of flour in the dried cranberries before chopping to keep them from clinging together. That worked beautifully. With the first batch, I remembered to subtract that amount of flour from the 2 c. the recipe calls for in the batter. The 2nd time I forgot. The 2nd batch turned out crumbly and didn't taste quite as good. That additional amount of flour made a noticeable difference in the texture of these delicious cookies. Oh, I used extra orange zest also--a whole orange worth, and cut back to 1 1/4 c. of dried cranberries.

These were wonderful. My husband was so disappointed when he realized there weren't any more left in the cookie jar! I'll have to make him another batch. I followed the recipe exactly, using the full 2 cups of craisins (which help balance the sweetness IMO) which I chopped quickly in the mini-processor and they were perfect. I had no trouble slicing them once they had been in the fridge. My bench scraper did the job easily by rocking it back and forth a bit. The dough was very forgiving if any slices needed re-rounding. Mine took 12 minutes but also were just a bit more browned than in the vid. I think the orange zest is crucial; if your zest isn't flavorful enough, use more. Personally I wouldn't add icing or the white chocolate chips to mine. Totally satisfying (and addicting I might add) as is.

I used the dried cranberries, dried cherries and white chocolate chips and used a lot of the orange zest. The flavor is SOOO good. Instead of "flouring" the dried cranberries, I pulsed the dried fruit for a few seconds in my blender, and the consistency works so well! It also makes the fruit burst with flavor! The only thing I noticed is they do crumble a bit after you take them out, but I'm going to put them in decorative muffin cup liners for a Christmas Cookie Exchange to prevent them from crumbling.

I LOVE these; but they are a bit too sweet. I think people don't realize that there's 28 grams of added sugar in most 40 grams of dried cranberries; they are meant to be tart but they are not. Also almond extract is very sweet. I cut some of the confectioner's sugar out and used reduced sugar cranberries for the second batch I made and it was PERFECTION. Best cookies ever I may never make a different cookie again.

I love these for the holidays. This year was my 2nd time making them. Although, this year I had more trouble than I remember having the previous time. Specifically at the step where you need to cut the cookies. For me they kept crumbling as I cut them due to the cranberries being tough. Is this a common issue? I had to reshape most of the cookies that I cut. They still came out great though! Was just frustrating. Also I made them vegan by using a plant based butter and they came out just as I remembered enjoying them the first time with real butter

Love this recipe. Couldn't be easier, they came out beautiful. Based on other reviews I used less cranberries, and chopped them up a bit before adding, also used orange extract as I had no almond extract. Wrapped them in parchment paper because it makes it easier to roll out into logs than plastic wrap or waxed paper since the dough is not stiff. Next time I will roll out to thinner logs before refrigerating to get smaller cookies. This recipe is a keeper. I am already planning variations on it.

My family loves these. They're a nice twist on shortbread & not overly sweet. I enjoy making them too. Like others suggested I just use 1 cup of dried cranberries, & only about 1/2 T of orange zest. My dough is not really dry, & once I loosely form the logs & wrap them in cling wrap I form the log into a nicer shape so that may make it more malleable. They slice & bake beautifully.
These cookies were a hit with my family. They were gone the same day. Instead of 3/4 cup confectioners sugar, I used 1/4 cup confectioners sugar and 1/2 cup Swerve (erythritol) sugar substitute.

I made these gluten free with King Arthur gf free all purpose flour and used Grand Marnier instead of the 1/2 tsp almond extract. I also added 1/2 cup pistachos so that they were Christmas cookies, with green and red bits! Lovely recipe, a keeper.
These are SO YUMMY and whoever I give them to rave about them. I've given out this recipe numerous times. I used half of the cranberries, and cooked them for about 15 minutes, not 10

Wonderful cookie with morning tea! Followed recipe, They melt in your mouth! I also tried with a drizzle of powdered sugar icing on top and it would be lovely for those who want something a bit sweeter for dessert.

First time making these and what a hit! I adjusted recipe to 2x and used half (2 cups) of cranberries and added 2 cups white chocolate chip. These make great gifts as well in a pretty seasonal container.
I thought these were delicious but I used about 1 cup of cranberries instead of 2 and added some walnuts.
Cookis are good, but a little sweet for me. Probably due to the added sugar from the dried cranberries. Next time I will reduce the sugar by 1/8-1/4 and see how they are
Great recipe, wonderful flavour and super easy!
My family from TX, AZ to CA beg for these easy to make, melt in your mouth cookies
These are a hit at every family gathering. We make them year round.
I used half the amount of dried cranberries as recommended by many others.
Made a few adjustments, added lime juice instead of orange and tart dried cherries - chopped up, instead of cranberries. Slight flavour change that I’m really enjoying.
